native.admission_inspect: Clouded ivory clasps a silk sleeve. The reed within is mute, yet a high thread of air worries the seam, as if a call had stopped one breath short.
apply_texts: Again the hush arrives one beat late. You cannot say what it nearly was. The ivory is cool, and cooler along the crack.
It happens again, too politely. Silk, high air, omission. You are not steadier for recognizing the order.
Little weight remains in the ivory. The high thread rises anyway, fails in its old place, and leaves the silk faintly proud.
The clasp turns a fraction and will not turn back. The same high fault repeats, stops, and leaves the reed exactly mute.
The habit is no longer delicate. The high omission arrives already complete in its failure, and courtesy does not soften it.
The loose thread catches your nail. For a moment the sleeve holds a finished high note, then offers only the gap where it should be.
The missing note does not arrive. In its place is a small, exact quiet. Your breath matches it, and the sleeve asks nothing.
The silk has creased into a habit. Each handling finds the high omission already waiting, polite and unfinished.
You turn the clasp. A high thread slips the seam and dies. The reed was never played; the silk remembers a pressure anyway.
inspect_texts: A single thread stands off the silk. You nearly name the high interval it sketches, then the clasp cools and the name fails.
Clouded ivory clasps a silk sleeve. The reed within is mute, yet a high thread of air worries the seam, as if a call had stopped one breath short.
One thread has left the seam. The ivory clasp is warm on one side only. Whatever note belongs here remains unsaid.
The omission is too precise to be wear. A high tone fails at the same place, and the clasp keeps a courtesy it was not given.
The silk sleeve is too fine for your hands. Its mute reed ticks once against ivory, a high small sound with no mouth behind it.
The sleeve repeats its small fault: silk, then a high hush, then nothing. The repetition is neat, and that neatness is the wrong part.
You almost place the missing interval. The reed stays mute. The silk, however, has learned the shape of a high call it does not finish.
native.name: Pallid Reed Sleeve
